key_insight: Time-weighted inequalities linking derivative norms identify conditions under which analyticity dominates intense-flow sparseness, excluding a class of strongly turbulent blow-up scenarios.
engineering_relevance: Higher-order derivative ratios offer a mathematical framework for interpreting turbulence scales and the onset of dissipation in three-dimensional flows.
method: Introduce time-weighted bridge inequalities between lower- and higher-order derivative norms.
Compare the analyticity radius with the sparseness scale of intense-flow regions.
Apply a harmonic-measure maximum principle to obtain norm contraction and analytic continuation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical regularity result for unforced 3D Navier–Stokes flows, with no numerical simulations or experimental validation described.
watch_item: The result excludes a specific class of blow-up scenarios under the stated scale conditions; it does not establish unconditional global regularity.
paper_title: Dynamic Interpolation and Higher-Order Turbulence Scales in 3D Navier-Stokes Flows
